author: reek
body: An AUTHENTICATED DTLS 1.3 handshake, end to end, over datagrams, with no network -- and the negative that proves it is authentication and not decoration.

author: reek
body: The server presents a real Ed25519 leaf certificate and signs the transcript with its private key. The certificate chain was minted outside Codex: the DER was built by .NET's ASN.1 writer and the signatures by our own RFC-8032-gated Ed25519 (the forge in scratchpad/forge). The client carries the CA as its trust anchor.

author: reek
body: UNLIKE THE ANONYMOUS LOOPBACK, THIS ONE AUTHENTICATES. If test-mitm below is not "not-done", the man-in-the-middle defence is broken and nothing here is secure.

author: reek
body: The handshake Randoms: caller-supplied entropy, fixed here for a reproducible exchange, distinct from the private keys.

author: reek
body: The trust anchor is the CA: parse its certificate, take its subject name and key. A name match alone means nothing here -- the anchor carries the KEY, and the leaf must be signed by it.

author: reek
body: The server presents the leaf and signs with the leaf's private key. The client requires authentication because it holds anchors.

author: reek
body: The cookie verifies: the server emits ServerHello, Certificate, CertificateVerify, Finished -- four datagrams.

author: reek
body: The client consumes them in order: ServerHello (keys), Certificate (chain walk), CertificateVerify (signature over its own transcript), Finished.

author: reek
body: The line that separates this from the anonymous loopback: the client authenticated the server.

target: section:A Client That Does Not Check
author: reek
body: The same certificate-presenting server, and a client with NO anchors. It does not require authentication and cannot verify the chain, so it keeps no peer key and ends unauthenticated -- but it must COMPLETE, because completing is a property of the transcript and the key schedule.

author: reek
body: This is the configuration the anonymous loopback cannot reach (an anonymous server sends no Certificate at all) and it is the ordinary one on the open internet. It could not complete until the Certificate and CertificateVerify messages folded into the transcript unconditionally: an unfolded message left this client's transcript one short of the server's and the server Finished failed to verify.

author: reek
body: Flip a byte 6 from the end -- inside the key_share value, past its length framing, so the ServerHello still parses and the failure lands at CertificateVerify rather than at ServerHello parsing.

author: reek
body: An ANONYMOUS server -- no certificate -- talking to a client that requires authentication. The server sends only ServerHello and Finished. The client has anchors, so it must refuse to complete rather than silently accept an unauthenticated peer.

author: reek
body: The chain proves the leaf is trusted; it does not prove it is the peer the client meant to reach. A client that pins the expected peer completes only when the leaf's subject is that peer, and refuses an otherwise-valid chain that authenticates a DIFFERENT holder under the same CA -- a man-in-the-middle holding a real certificate of his own.

author: reek
body: The wrong-host client is built from the start rather than adjusted mid-handshake, because the expected name is now a property the endpoint is CONSTRUCTED with and not one that can be set afterwards. Same key, same random, same anchors, same server datagrams -- the only difference is the name it says it dialled, which is exactly the variable under test.

author: reek
body: The chain still walks to the anchor and every signature still verifies. The leaf is genuinely `device.codex.test`, and this client asked for `evil.codex.test`, so it must not authenticate and must not complete.
